text:
Anya P.: infra-bot fired an alert for high memory on us-central1-pool-4 during a cross-region rebalance. Creating a thread to capture root cause and mitigation notes.

infra-bot: ALERT: node=us-central1-gpu-27 memory_use=95% oom_count=3 window=5m

Sam K.: saw this start right after the rebalancer run at ~03:12 UTC. lots of sessions moved into the pool.

Devin R.: confirming — KV cache per-session size spiked after migration. looks like a duplicate-upsert from the rebalancer combined with the ttl-default bug in kv-service v2.8.1. Evictions never triggered.

Maria L.: logs showing the sequence:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:04Z rebalancer: started migration batch=142 shards=18
2026-03-15T03:12:12Z kv-cache: insert session=abc123 size=1.2MB ttl=0
2026-03-15T03:12:36Z node=us-central1-gpu-27 mem=92% throttle=soft
2026-03-15T03:13:01Z kv-cache: insert session=def456 size=0.9MB ttl=0
2026-03-15T03:13:22Z autoscaler: quota_check=0.5_gpus_available reason=reserved_capacity
```

Sam K.: autoscaler refused to scale because we had reserved Dedicated capacity in that region and the quota call returned low available GPU hours. combined effect = no headroom.

Devin R.: root cause summary: (1) rebalancer duplicate-upsert bug caused extreme per-session KV growth; (2) kv-service TTL defaulted to 0 for migrated entries so eviction policy skipped them; (3) autoscaler headroom was constrained by reserved quotas -> nodes filled up -> router began soft-throttling requests which pushed p99 latencies up.

Jordan (ops): additional constraint: we disabled preemptible-burst on that pool last month to stabilize costs for a sales demo. that removed an emergency source of capacity.

Anya P.: immediate actions: 1) hotfix rebalancer to avoid duplicate-upsert (owner: Devin) 2) force-evict stale/migrated KV on affected nodes (owner: Sam) 3) temporary enable emergency preemptible burst for this pool and request quota bump (owner: Jordan) 4) add safe default TTL for migrated entries (owner: Maria) 5) update forecasting to include rebalancer-induced short bursts (owner: Devin)

Devin R.: pushing hotfix branch now, will roll a canary to us-central1-pool-4 in ~10m. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rebalancer/pull/480 (canary artifacts published) :thumbsup:

Sam K.: running eviction script: `/scripts/kv_evict --filter pool=us-central1-pool-4 --dry-run` then live. running live now, will post results.

deploy-bot: DEPLOY: canary deployed to us-central1-pool-4 by deploy-bot at 03:42 UTC

infra-bot: NOTE: post-eviction memory samples: nodes [gpu-24,gpu-25,gpu-27] dropped from avg 91% -> 54% within 6m

Maria L.: verified: no more throttle logs after eviction and hotfix applied to canary. rolling to remainder of pool now.

Jordan (ops): follow-ups: filing quota request with cloud provider (case #CLD-8891) and scheduling re-enable of emergency preemptible-burst toggle for pools with reserved capacity. also rework alert thresholds for rebalance windows.

Anya P.: quick postmortem notes to include: - cause chain (rebalancer upsert bug -> ttl=0 eviction bypass -> reserved quota headroom gap) - mitigation timeline and rollouts - short-term config changes (ttl default, emergency burst toggle) - forecasting change (treat rebalances as 5-15m burst with 2-3x session KV factor) - action owners and deadlines. assigning postmortem doc to Devin (target: draft by EOD tomorrow).

Devin R.: I'll draft the postmortem and include load reproducer + perf numbers. goal: add automated fallback that triggers KV trim when mem>80% during rebalance windows.

Sam K.: leaving notes for runbook update: add `kv_evict` runbook entry + link to eviction script + safe dry-run steps.

Maria L.: will add a test to CI that ensures TTL is set on migrated entries and that eviction queue sees them within 30s.

Jordan (ops): once postmortem is up, we should revisit cost policy for disabling preemptible bursts. the cost saved last month wasn't worth the availability hit.

Anya P.: thanks team — this thread will be the basis for the formal postmortem. assigning owners in the doc now. :white_check_mark:
